package lang // import "github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/pkg/lang"

Package lang reads source files and configuration into facts: symbols,
references, refused references and the facts a dialect declares, each with the
level that readings measured for the dialect that read it.

Bytes and a path go in. Nothing else is needed: no store, no daemon, no index,
no git and no network. A Reader is safe for concurrent use and deterministic:
equal inputs give byte-equal JSON.

The package is a door over fathom's own extraction code (ADR-092). Public
types are defined here, so a change inside fathom does not change this API.
Symbol.Canonical is a closed vocabulary that only grows; Symbol.Kind is each
dialect's own name and may change as a language improves.

The wazero runtime that runs the grammars is process-wide, so its on-disk
compilation cache is a package function, EnableCompilationCache, and is off by
default. Without it the package writes no file.

CONSTANTS

const (
	PackEmpty      = extractor.PackEmpty      // the pack holds no dialect
	PackManifest   = extractor.PackManifest   // a manifest is unreadable or breaks the dialect rules
	PackConflict   = extractor.PackConflict   // an id, source kind, extension or basename is already taken
	PackEngine     = extractor.PackEngine     // the engine is not tags or doc
	PackInjections = extractor.PackInjections // queries.injections is not accepted in a pack
	PackGrammar    = extractor.PackGrammar    // the grammar is not one the library embeds
	PackQuery      = extractor.PackQuery      // a query does not compile against its grammar
	PackContainer  = extractor.PackContainer  // match.container is not accepted in a pack
	PackClaims     = extractor.PackClaims     // the dialect claims no file, or claims one by a shebang
	PackRoute      = extractor.PackRoute      // the dialect claims what a built-in dialect owns outright
)
    The reasons a pack or a Go extractor is refused, in PackError.Reason.
    The set is closed.

const (
	SkipBinary       = "binary"       // the bytes are not source text
	SkipOversize     = "oversize"     // over the file limit (2 MiB, lowerable by WithLimits)
	SkipGenerated    = "generated"    // a generated file the dialect excludes
	SkipAmbiguous    = "ambiguous"    // the file could belong to two dialects and the content does not settle it
	SkipUnclassified = "unclassified" // no dialect reads this path and content
	SkipNotLinked    = "not-linked"   // a dialect owns the file but its extractor is not linked into this Reader
)
    Skip reasons: the closed set Result.Skipped holds. A skipped file has no
    symbols; the reason says why.

const (
	LevelUnmeasured = "unmeasured" // no reading exists for the dialect
	LevelNone       = "none"       // measured, and no level was met
)
    Level values Result.Level and DialectInfo.Level hold besides L1 to L4.

const DefaultMaxFileBytes = langroute.MaxExtractSize
    DefaultMaxFileBytes is the largest file a Reader reads: the product's own
    limit. A larger file is skipped as oversize.


VARIABLES

var ErrClosed = errors.New("lang: reader is closed")
    ErrClosed is returned by Extract on a Reader that was closed.


FUNCTIONS

func EnableCompilationCache(dir string) error
    EnableCompilationCache turns on wazero's on-disk compilation cache for the
    process, under dir. It is off by default. The cache holds machine code the
    process will execute, so dir must be an absolute path that no group or other
    user can write; a directory that does not exist is created with mode 0700.
    It must be called before the first Reader is built, because the runtime is
    made once, and it errors on a second, different directory. Calling it again
    with the same directory is a no-op.


TYPES

type DialectInfo struct {
	ID string `json:"id"`
	// Kind is "language" or "tooling".
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Engine is how the dialect is read: tags, doc, tags+doc or native.
	Engine string `json:"engine"`
	// Matches is the sorted extensions, basenames and globs the dialect claims.
	Matches []string `json:"matches"`
	// Level and Grade are what readings proved: Level is L1 to L4, LevelNone
	// or LevelUnmeasured, Grade the grade at that level ("" when none).
	Level string `json:"level"`
	Grade string `json:"grade"`
}
    DialectInfo describes one dialect a Reader can read.

type Extracted struct {
	Symbols    []Symbol
	References []Reference
	Unresolved []Unresolved
	Facts      []Fact
}
    Extracted is what an Extractor reads from one file. Symbol.Key,
    Symbol.Canonical and Reference.ToKey are derived by the Reader and ignored
    here. Reference.Edge is the extractor's own relation name and is passed
    through.

type Extractor interface {
	Extract(ctx context.Context, f File) (Extracted, error)
}
    An Extractor reads the files a Match claims. It must be safe for concurrent
    use and deterministic. A panic in it is returned by Reader.Extract as an
    error.

type Fact struct {
	Entity string `json:"entity"`
	Key    string `json:"key"`
	Value  string `json:"value"`
	Line   int    `json:"line"`
}
    Fact is one scalar a dialect declares an entity writes.

type File struct {
	Path string
	Src  []byte
	// Siblings is the optional list of the other repository-relative paths in
	// the same repository. Some classifications read it (an Ansible role, a
	// Helm chart's templates, a Timoni module). Empty is legal: the file is
	// then classified alone, and Result.Notes says so when that could change
	// the verdict.
	Siblings []string
}
    File is one file to read. Path is repository-relative with forward slashes
    and is the only thing the Reader knows about where the file lives.

type Limits struct {
	// MaxFileBytes lowers the file size limit (DefaultMaxFileBytes).
	MaxFileBytes int
}
    Limits are the bounds a Reader works under. A zero field keeps the default.

type Match struct {
	// ID names the dialect: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and not a
	// dialect the Reader already has.
	ID string
	// Kind is "language" or "tooling" ("language" when empty).
	Kind string
	// Extensions (with their dot), Basenames and Globs claim files, as in a pack.
	// A built-in dialect's extension or basename is refused.
	Extensions []string
	Basenames  []string
	Globs      []string
	// Sniff claims files by content.
	Sniff *Sniff
	// Kinds maps each Symbol.Kind the extractor emits to its Symbol.Canonical,
	// a value of the closed vocabulary. At least one is required.
	Kinds map[string]string
}
    Match says which files a Go extractor reads and which kinds it emits.
    It is held to the rules a pack dialect is.

type Option func(*config) error
    Option configures New.

func Link(family string) Option
    Link adds an extractor family a sibling package registers by import, by its
    name. Use that package's Option (pkg/lang/cue.Option) rather than calling
    Link. New returns an error when the family's package was not imported.

func WithDialects(fsys fs.FS) Option
    WithDialects adds a pack: dialects read from fsys, laid out as
    dialects/<id>/dialect.json beside the queries and doc specs each names.
    A pack is data. It names a grammar the library embeds and runs no code of
    its own, and only the "tags" and "doc" engines are accepted.

    The pack is merged with the built-in dialects and held to the same rules
    they are, then compiled, and New returns a *PackError and no Reader when any
    dialect breaks one. A pack dialect claims files by basename, glob or sniff,
    or by an extension no built-in dialect owns. It is tried after the specific
    built-in dialects and before an extension's generic reader, in id order,
    so it cannot take a file a built-in dialect reads. Its queries run under the
    same budget as the built-ins'. A pack dialect's Level is LevelUnmeasured.
    queries.injections is not accepted in this version.

    pkg/lang/langtest.CheckPack runs the same checks, then the pack's goldens.

func WithExtractor(m Match, e Extractor) Option
    WithExtractor registers a Go extractor under the same routing rules as a
    pack dialect: it is merged with the built-ins, tried in id order after the
    specific built-ins and before an extension's generic reader, and refused
    whole, as a *PackError, when it breaks a rule. Its dialect appears in
    Dialects with Engine "native" and Level LevelUnmeasured.

func WithLimits(l Limits) Option
    WithLimits lowers the Reader's limits. A limit above the product's, or a
    negative one, is an error: no option raises a limit, and no option raises a
    grammar module's memory cap.

type PackError struct {
	// Reason is one of the Pack constants.
	Reason string
	// Dialect is the dialect that broke the rule, "" when the pack as a whole did.
	Dialect string
	// Detail says which rule and why.
	Detail string
}
    PackError is why New refused a pack or a Go extractor. Nothing of it is
    loaded: a pack is accepted whole or not at all.

func (e *PackError) Error() string

type Reader struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Reader reads files into facts. Build one with New and Close it. A Reader is
    safe for concurrent use.

func New(opts ...Option) (r *Reader, err error)
    New builds a Reader. It returns the error a bad option or a bad built-in
    dialect gives, and never panics. The Reader links every built-in dialect
    except CUE and Timoni, which a consumer adds by importing pkg/lang/cue.

func (r *Reader) Close() error
    Close releases the Reader's pooled grammar modules. It is idempotent,
    and waits for extractions in flight.

func (r *Reader) Dialects() []DialectInfo
    Dialects lists every dialect the Reader reads, sorted by id, with the level
    and grade that readings measured for it.

func (r *Reader) Extract(ctx context.Context, f File) (Result, error)
    Extract reads one file. A file no dialect reads is not an error:
    the Result says why in Skipped. The error is for misuse (an empty path,
    a closed Reader, a done context). A file an extractor could not fully read
    returns what it did read, and Notes says what failed.

type Reference struct {
	// From is the Key of the referencing symbol, or "" for a reference the
	// document itself makes.
	From string `json:"from"`
	// To is the target exactly as the dialect names it: a Go call names
	// package.Func, a Terraform reference var.name, a CloudFormation Ref the
	// logical id, a cross-file reference the path, image or address the
	// Strategy resolved. It is not necessarily a Key.
	To string `json:"to"`
	// ToKey is the Key of the symbol in the same file that To names, when To
	// equals exactly one symbol's Key or Name, and empty otherwise (a target
	// in another file, an ambiguous name, a cross-file reference).
	ToKey string `json:"to_key"`
	// Edge names the relation: "call" for a call, "reference" for a plain
	// reference from a document dialect that declares no relation, and
	// otherwise the edge the dialect declares (uses, imports, depends_on and
	// so on). Do not branch on an Edge across dialects.
	Edge string `json:"edge"`
	// Raw is the value as written, when it differs from To.
	Raw string `json:"raw"`
	// Strategy is how a document reference resolved (repo-path, image-ref,
	// module-source and so on), empty for a call.
	Strategy string `json:"strategy"`
	// Line is the line the reference is written on. 0 means the engine does
	// not record one: calls read by the tree-sitter and Go engines carry no
	// line.
	Line int `json:"line"`
}
    Reference is one edge from a symbol (or the document, From "") to a target.

type Result struct {
	// Dialect is the id of the dialect that read the file ("" when none did).
	Dialect string `json:"dialect"`
	// Language is the file's language class from its path.
	Language string `json:"language"`
	// Skipped is a Skip reason, or "" when a dialect read the file.
	Skipped    string       `json:"skipped"`
	Symbols    []Symbol     `json:"symbols"`
	References []Reference  `json:"references"`
	Unresolved []Unresolved `json:"unresolved"`
	Facts      []Fact       `json:"facts"`
	// Level is the dialect's measured level: L1 to L4, LevelNone or
	// LevelUnmeasured. It is what readings proved about the dialect, not a
	// promise about this file.
	Level string `json:"level"`
	// Incomplete is true when an engine could not fully read the file: the
	// symbols, references and facts above are what it did read, and Notes says
	// why. False means no engine reported a failure, which is not a promise
	// that every construct was read: the tree-sitter dialects recover from a
	// syntax error without reporting it. A policy tool that must not pass a
	// file it could not read should refuse when Incomplete is true.
	Incomplete bool `json:"incomplete"`
	// Notes disclose what the Reader could not know and that may have changed
	// the result. Empty when nothing did.
	Notes []string `json:"notes"`
}
    Result is what one file holds. Every slice is non-nil and sorted, so equal
    inputs give byte-equal JSON.

type Sniff struct {
	Extensions []string
	Pattern    string
}
    Sniff claims files of the listed extensions whose first kilobyte matches
    Pattern (a Go regular expression, matched across lines).

type Symbol struct {
	// Key is the symbol's identity within its file: Package and Name joined by
	// a dot, or Name alone when Package is empty. Reference.From and
	// Reference.ToKey hold Keys. A dialect names a reference target as it
	// writes it (Reference.To), which equals a Key only when the dialect
	// writes targets the way it names definitions; ToKey is the join.
	Key     string `json:"key"`
	Name    string `json:"name"`
	Package string `json:"package"`
	// Kind is the dialect's own name for what the symbol is (for example
	// TerraformResource). Kinds may be added and renamed as languages
	// improve; do not branch on a Kind across dialects.
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Canonical is the closed cross-dialect vocabulary. Values only grow. It
	// is empty for a kind no dialect manifest declares.
	Canonical string `json:"canonical"`
	Line      int    `json:"line"`
	// EndLine is the last line, 0 when the extractor does not compute it.
	EndLine   int    `json:"end_line"`
	Signature string `json:"signature"`
	// Tier is how the symbol was established: verified, pre-scan,
	// doc-claimed, sme-stated or assumed.
	Tier string `json:"tier"`
}
    Symbol is one definition.

type Unresolved struct {
	From   string `json:"from"`
	Edge   string `json:"edge"`
	Raw    string `json:"raw"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
	Line   int    `json:"line"`
}
    Unresolved is a reference the Reader read and refused to guess.
